title: Arrays & Two Pointers
description: Drawn from practiced problems: 3Sum, Container With Most Water, Move Zeroes, Climbing Stairs, Remove Covered Intervals.

questions.prompt: After sorting the input, what is the time complexity of the standard two-pointer 3Sum solution?
questions.explanation: Fix one element (O(n)) and run a two-pointer scan over the rest (O(n)) -> O(n^2); sorting's O(n log n) is dominated.

questions.prompt: In Container With Most Water, which pointer do you move to have any chance of a larger area?

options: Move the pointer at the taller line inward
Move the pointer at the shorter line inward
Move both pointers inward every step

questions.explanation: Area is bounded by the shorter line; moving the taller one can only shrink width without lifting the bound, so move the shorter one.

questions.prompt: Move Zeroes can be solved in-place with O(1) extra space using a write index.
questions.explanation: Keep a write pointer for the next non-zero slot; swap/overwrite as you scan. No extra array needed.

questions.prompt: Climbing Stairs (1 or 2 steps) counts the same as which classic integer sequence?
questions.explanation: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2), the Fibonacci recurrence.

questions.prompt: To detect covered intervals efficiently in Remove Covered Intervals, how should you sort first?

options: Start ascending, then end descending on ties
End ascending, then start ascending on ties

questions.explanation: Sorting start ascending and end descending on equal starts guarantees a covering interval appears before the one it covers, so a single end-pointer sweep works.
